chunks: And upon you be peace, and know that He says: 'Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out.'

From the tribulations, and a light from the darkness, and will keep him forever in what his soul desires, and will place him in a position of honor near Him, in a house He has made for Himself, whose shade is His Throne, whose light is His joy, whose visitors are His angels, and whose companions are His prophets.
So hasten to the Return, and race against the death, for indeed people will soon have their hope cut off, and death will overtake them, and the door of repentance will be closed to them,

You have become in a state like that to which those before you wished to return. You are travelers, on a journey from a house that is not your home, and you have been given permission to leave from it, and ordered to take provision while in it.

key_terms.الزَّادِ: provision or supplies for the journey

ai.seo_question: How does fearing Allah provide an escape from tribulations according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali links the Quranic promise of 'a way out' (65:2) to the concept of *Fitna* (tribulation), emphasizing that God-consciousness provides both spiritual illumination and a physical escape from worldly trials. This passage, found in the section on the Quran's virtues, underscores the transient nature of the world (*Dar al-Ghurur*) and urges believers to treat life as a journey requiring spiritual provisions (*Zad*) before the 'door of repentance' closes.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You should know that whoever fears Allāh, He would make for him a way to get out of troubles and (grant him) a light (to help him) out of darkness.

He will ever keep him in what ever (condition) he wishes, and will make him stay in a position of honour near Himself, in the house which He has made for Himself. The shade of this house is His throne, its light is His effulgence, its visitors are His angels and its companions are His prophets.

Therefore, hasten towards the place of return and go ahead of (your) deaths (by collecting provision for the next world). Shortly, the expectations of the people will be cut short and death will overtake them while the door of repentance will be closed for them.

You are still in a place to which those who were before you have been wishing to return. In this world, which is not your house, you are just a traveller in motion. You have been given the call to leave from here, and you have been ordered to collect provision while you are here.
